Heard learned counsel for the applicant and the learned A.G.A.
The present application has been filed seeking bail in Case Crime No. 69 of 2023 under Sections 498A and 304-B, I.P.C., and Section 3/4, Dowry Prohibition Act, P.S. Jagdishpur, District Amethi.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits that P.W. 1, father of the deceased, was examined before the trial court and he deposed that day before the death of his daughter his wife had gone to her sasural and his daughter had told that her health was not proper and she was taking medicine for long time and she wished to die.
His wife pacified her and came back to house.
Later on, on the said date it was informed that his daughter had locked door from inside and it was found that she was lying dead.
The door was broken and it was found that the dead-body was hanging from the fan.

Lastly he has been declared 'hostile'.

Learned counsel for the applicant has filed supplementary affidavit today, bringing on record statement of P.W.-2, mother of the deceased, which indicates that she has been declared 'hostile'.
It has been submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that after looking into statements of the P.W.1 and P.W.2/father and mother of the deceased, it cannot be inferred that the applicant was involved in commission of the said offence.
The applicant is in jail since 13.03.2023 and he has no criminal history.
Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail, but has not disputed the aforesaid facts.
Considering overall facts and circumstances of the case and also the fact that P.W.-1 and P.W.2 have turned hostile, it is a fit case for bail.

Let the applicant Jaseem, involved in aforesaid case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation,
then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law,
under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
(Brij Raj Singh, J.) Order Date :- 7.11.2024
